Step 48: Configure Distinct Until Changed
↑ top

Register Distinct Until Changed with operators() in example.service.ts. The operator evaluates the resolved and merged candidate before filters and reducers, then suppresses a candidate that the comparison considers unchanged.

This is the only functional update in the example. The component and template changes only provide buttons and a read-only comparison-function view so you can observe the configured behavior.

Take Action
  1. Install the package.
  2. Open example.service.ts.
  3. Import and register withDistinctUntilChanged() through this.#vault.operators().
  4. Review the identity comparison that accepts a candidate only when it introduces a new character ID. 
npm install @sdux-vault/addons
What to Look For
  • Operators run after Resolve and Merge, before filters and reducers.
  • The first candidate proceeds; later equivalent candidates stop at the Operator stage.
  • The comparison function textarea is observational only. It does not execute from the component or template.

Step 49: Submit Same and Changed State
↑ top

Select Submit Same State to reconstruct Rey as a new object and merge it into the collection. The first new identity is accepted; later Rey submissions contain no new ID, so the comparison suppresses the candidate even though the object was newly allocated.

Select Submit Changed State to cycle through four distinct Jedi. Each new identity proceeds through the pipeline and updates State. After the cycle wraps, repeated identities are suppressed without relying on collection order.

Take Action
  1. Select Submit Same State twice and observe that only the first accepted identity changes State.
  2. Select Submit Changed State through the four-character cycle.
  3. Inspect the Comparison Function textarea as you compare the visible collection with each request.
What to Look For
  • Both buttons delegate to the service; they do not implement comparison logic in the component.
  • Suppressed candidates do not continue to downstream filter or reducer stages.
  • The comparison function is displayed solely to explain the service configuration.

Step 50: Complete Distinct Until Changed Tutorial
↑ top

Your example is complete when the service registers the distinct operator, repeated identities are suppressed before downstream stages, and new identities continue to update FeatureCell State. The buttons and comparison textarea make that service-owned decision visible without taking over the operator's work.

What to Look For
  • Distinctness is defined by the configured comparison function, not object allocation or collection position.
  • The service owns the operator registration and State updates.
  • The component and template remain presentation-only for this teaching view.
